Resolves #20212

`TreeStore#splice()` no longer scans the projection once per removed node. Step 1b decides visibility with `map.has(key)` instead of `indexOf()`. A removal of the whole projection (`clear()`, a data reload) reaches the Collection in its numeric form, which drops the projection in one pass. Clearing and reloading are now linear in the visible node count.

Evidence: L1 (unit tier in Node) → L1 required (AC-1 to AC-4 are unit-level; AC-4's timings come from a unit probe, below).

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | `test/playwright/unit/data/TreeStoreClear.spec.mjs`: the flat and the expanded arm count zero `indexOf` / `indexOfKey` calls during `clear()` (red on `dev`: 1,500 and 1,530) |
| AC-2 | same spec: `clear()` empties both layers and its `mutate` reports the removed projection in order; a data reload replaces the previous tree (green on `dev` and here) |
| AC-3 | the full unit tier on this branch: 5,652 passed, 2 skipped; CI runs it again |
| AC-4 | the timing table under `## Test Evidence`, measured at this head |

## Test Evidence
A timing probe (Turbo Mode, Node, ms), run back to back on `dev` `4de3f3cda8` and on this branch:

| Case | `dev` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 10,000 flat visible nodes, `clear()` | 91 | 5 |
| 20,000 flat visible nodes, `clear()` | 752 | 9 |
| 40,000 flat visible nodes, `clear()` | 2,122 | 20 |
| 50 × 800 expanded (40,050 visible), `clear()` | 1,127 | 26 |
| 40,000 flat, `store.data = rows` | 2,246 | 99 |
| `Store`, 40,000 rows, `clear()` (control) | 0 | 0 |
| 50 × 800 collapsed (50 visible), `clear()` (control) | 1 | 0 |

Red-first: the two scan arms fail on `dev` and pass here. The two preservation arms pass on both.

Prescription checked: `src/data/TreeStore.mjs` owns the concern. Its `splice()` override turns the Collection's one-pass numeric removal into a per-item array removal, so handing a full removal back in numeric form is its job. An O(N) array removal in `Collection#splice()` would be broader, covering every Store, and #20212 keeps it out of scope.

## Comments

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-11-03T05:58:55Z

Follow-up: this change routes `TreeStore` full removals through the Collection's numeric `splice` path, and that path loses items added in the same call. A tree replace-all, `splice(0, count, newNodes)`, therefore ends empty on `dev` since this merge. Julia caught it in her review's defect-note. The root cause is in `Collection#splice` and predates this PR. It is filed as #20217 and fixed in #20218, with red-first arms for `Collection` and `TreeStore`.

# PR Review Summary

**Status:** Approved

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

Per §9 Strategic-Fit Step-Back:
- **Decision**: Approve
- **Rationale**: `TreeStore#splice()` is the exact owner of the two $O(V^2)$ projection-scan bottlenecks during `clear()` and `store.data = rows` reloads (`#20212`). Replacing `me.indexOf(node) > -1` with `me.map.has(key)` in Step 1b eliminates the per-node `_items` scan ($O(1)$ hash lookup against the visible projection map), and delegating full-projection removals (`index === 0 && removeCountOrToRemoveArray === me.count`) in numeric form `super.splice(0, me.count, visibleToAdd, silent)` allows `Collection#splice()` to execute its one-pass `map.clear()` + `me._items = []` branch (`src/collection/Base.mjs:1576-1580`) instead of `items.splice(me.indexOfKey(key), 1)` per node. Merge-safe with 0 Required Actions.

**Peer-Review Opening:** Nice catch isolating both quadratic paths in `TreeStore#splice()` and backing the fix with both a zero-scan structural assertion (`countScans` on `indexOf` / `indexOfKey`) and back-to-back 10k/20k/40k timing measurements (`2,122 ms` -> `20 ms` on 40k flat `clear()`, `1,127 ms` -> `26 ms` on 40k expanded `clear()`, and `2,246 ms` -> `99 ms` on 40k reload).
